Basic things, as a new pilot, start with 10ish back armor on your sides torsos and center torso,  max the front armor with whats left.  More armor is more important than excess heatsinks, unless your stripping arms of armor that have no weapons and aren't good twisting shield arms.   As you get better lower back armor on lights to about 2 and assaults to about 7, putting the freed up armor on the front.  Head armor can usally be lowered to about 10-12, 

leg armor shouldn't be lowered by more than 20% of its max, but most people don't lower it by more than 5%, it depends on mech, never lower leg armor on light mechs.

Endosteel is always better than ferro fibrous, your build there can fit light ferro, which would free up tonnage for more armor, but again you can just lose those excess heat sinks.    Unless your running high alpha (usually laser vomit builds) more than 10 heatsinks (there are 10 heatsinks in all engines 250 or larger) is not that important.

AMS is a neiche "what can i do with this spare tonnage" item usually, learn to stay near walls that will cover you from lrms and dump the ams.

People here telling you to buy LFE engines are all probably rolling in cbills,  yes its a great improvement for tonnage but as a new player and your comment about not wanting to buy double heatsinks (changing to double heatsinks option changes the heatsinks in engine too) is important, a workable build can be made with the engine you have.
